summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — RTO.L +7%, QIA.DE +6%, LSEG.L +3%, AZN.L +3%, BN.PA +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (RMS.PA -8%, ASM.AS -6%, AAL.L -5%, ANTO.L -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: RMS.PA (-7.71%) — Q3 sales (reported Oct 22) rose only 4.3% at constant currency vs ~5.2% expected. Asia was flat, ready-to-wear fell 2% and watches fell 6%, which sparked a luxury-sector derating. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: RMS.PA is a ~€130B+ euro-denominated Paris large cap, and no strategy includes it. The move was also a scheduled-results gap, which pre-market positioning and earnings gates would have left to settle before any signal.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely the Q3 2026 trading update (Rentokil reports in late October). I couldn't find coverage of today's update, so this is inferred from its past Q3 updates, which sent the shares up 9–10%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RTO.L is a UK mid-cap (FTSE 100/250 borderline) pest-control and hygiene services stock. A scheduled morning RNS gap-up is also over before post-open momentum signals fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100/250 constituents (RTO.L included) to the news-reactive universe, and release the earnings gate for names that gap up ≥ +5% on a trading-update RNS within 30 minutes of the 07:00 UK open.

top_movers.catalyst: EQT-led consortium takeover offer for Qiagen at €46.50/share in cash (~€10.8B), backed by Qiagen's boards. The stock is converging on the offer price. Coverage dates are fuzzy, so today's move may be a follow-through.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a mid/large-cap German diagnostics name that none of the strategies cover. It is also a deal-driven jump with the price pinned just under the €46.50 offer, which momentum and mean-reversion filters wouldn't take.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an M&A-arb watchlist (not a momentum entry) that flags names with a firm cash offer and a spread to the offer of 2–5%. Keep it separate from the momentum-trader gap-up logic and size it small, given the deal runs to mid-2027.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up only routine buyback notices, so this looks like a technical rebound or sector move after a long drawdown (about -22% over the past year).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LSEG is a ~£40B FTSE 100 financial-data and exchange name that no strategy lists. A +3% move with no catalyst also wouldn't pass a news-reactive or gap-up filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 large caps to the momentum universe, or add a daily scan of non-universe names with a close-to-close move of at least +3% on volume of at least 1.5x average, to flag candidates for review.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-23 (searches returned nothing dated that day) — likely a large-cap pharma/sector rebound after a ~5% weekly pullback.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AZN.L is a ~£150B+ FTSE 100 mega-cap pharma that no strategy lists. A steady +2.6% large-cap move with no gap or volume spike would also fail typical momentum and gap-up filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 mega-caps to the momentum universe with a relative-strength trigger (e.g. +2% day with volume ≥1.2× 20-day average) and a low position cap, so liquid defensives like AZN.L are screened.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Danone's Q3 sales are due Oct 28, so this looks like a pre-results run-up or a rotation into European staples.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BN.PA is a large-cap Euronext Paris consumer-staples name, and a +2.4% move in a low-beta defensive likely wouldn't pass momentum, gap or volume-spike filters even if it were included.
top_movers.suggestion: Add CAC 40 / Euro Stoxx 50 staples (BN.PA, OR.PA, etc.) to the momentum universe with a relative-strength-vs-sector trigger, since a fixed +3% gap threshold would still skip +2.4% moves in low-vol names.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-23 — searches returned no dated Admiral news, so likely a technical or sector move (UK insurers/financials), not a stock-specific event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ADM.L is a FTSE 100 UK non-life insurer, a defensive financial that no strategy lists. A +2.39% drift with no catalyst would also be too small for gap-up or news-reactive triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK/EU large-cap financials sleeve (e.g. ADM.L, LGEN.L, PHNX.L) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a sector-relative move of at least +2% against the FTSE 350 Insurance index. Skip this if the strategy can't hold sub-3% movers.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 sales (reported Oct 22) rose only 4.3% at constant currency vs ~5.2% expected. Asia was flat, ready-to-wear fell 2% and watches fell 6%, which sparked a luxury-sector derating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RMS.PA is a ~€130B+ euro-denominated Paris large cap, and no strategy includes it. The move was also a scheduled-results gap, which pre-market positioning and earnings gates would have left to settle before any signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add CAC40 luxury names (RMS.PA, MC.PA, KER.PA) to the news-reactive universe and let its earnings gate release names with a post-results gap ≤ -5% on volume ≥1.5× average, or log them as a no-trade if shorting is unavailable.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst found. ASM's Q3 results are normally late Oct, so this is likely a semi-equipment sector de-rating or pre-earnings positioning (unverified).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM International is a Euronext Amsterdam mid/large-cap semi-equipment name that no strategy covers. A sector drift with no single-name gap would also fail gap and volume triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add ASM.AS, together with ASML.AS, BESI.AS and AIXA.DE, to the uk-eu momentum universe as a semi-equipment basket. Then flag any basket day with a median move of -3% or worse as a sector-move alert.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. The likely cause is Anglo American's Q3 production report, usually published in late October, or weakness in metals and the FTSE miners. I could not verify either.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AAL.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap diversified miner that no uk-eu strategy covers. A -5% drop from a scheduled production update or a sector move is also not something a momentum or mean-reversion filter would flag in advance.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 miners (AAL.L, GLEN.L, RIO.L, ANTO.L) to the mean-reversion universe, and add a sector-wide filter that flags when ≥3 of them fall more than 3% on the same day.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear Oct 23 news found. Likely continued fallout from the Oct 15 Q3 update (copper and gold missed consensus, 2027 guidance soft, 2026 cash-cost guidance raised) plus a copper/miners move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ANTO.L is a FTSE 100 Chile-focused copper miner that no strategy lists. With no same-day catalyst, a -4.87% drift in a mining name would also fit poorly with news-reactive triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 miners (ANTO.L, GLEN.L, RIO.L) to the mean-reversion universe, with a copper-futures sector-move filter (e.g. entry only when LME copper is down ≥2% on the day) to separate sector moves from stock-specific ones.
